from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["The dot product measures the projection of vectors.", "Visualize it as a shadow cast by light.", "It captures how much vectors align together.", "Think of a hiker climbing a steep hill.", "Only the upward motion contributes to the work."]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Intuition: The Projection", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        line = Line(start=self.grid["E1"], end=self.grid["E6"], color=WHITE)
        vec_a = Vector([1.5, 1.2], color=YELLOW)
        vec_a.shift(self.grid["D3"] - vec_a.get_start())
        
        # Project vector a onto line (assuming line is horizontal)
        projection_point = np.array([vec_a.get_end()[0], self.grid["E3"][1], 0])
        projection_line = DashedLine(start=vec_a.get_end(), end=projection_point, color=GRAY)
        projection_vector = Line(start=self.grid["E3"], end=projection_point, color="#FF5733", stroke_width=6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(line), Create(vec_a))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(projection_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(projection_vector))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        # Hiker logic representation
        hiker = Dot(color=GREEN).move_to(vec_a.get_end())
        self.play(FadeIn(hiker))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Indicate(projection_vector))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Algebraically, the dot product relates length and angle.",
            "The formula is magnitude times cosine of theta.",
            "It bridges geometry with specific coordinate values."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Algebraic Bridge", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        formula = MathTex(r"a \cdot b = |a| |b| \cos(\theta)")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show the formula
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight components (magnitude, cosine)
        mag_a = formula[0][5:8]
        mag_b = formula[0][9:12]
        cos_theta = formula[0][12:18]
        
        self.play(
            mag_a.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            mag_b.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            cos_theta.animate.set_color(BLUE)
        )
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight result value
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "View the dot product as a linear function.",
            "A fixed vector acts as a measurement machine.",
            "It transforms any input vector into a scalar.",
            "This perspective introduces the dual space concept.",
            "Imagine a security camera sensing incoming motion."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core of Duality: Vectors as Functions", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors for lines
        colors = ["#FFD700", "#00FFFF", "#FF4500", "#7FFF00", "#FF69B4"]

        # Define Mobjects
        vector_v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=colors[1])
        vector_x = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=colors[2])
        function_label = MathTex(r"f(\vec{x}) = \vec{v} \cdot \vec{x}", color=colors[0])
        camera_icon = Square(color=colors[4], fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(colors[0])
        self.place_at_grid(function_label, "B2")
        self.play(Write(function_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        self.place_at_grid(vector_v, "D2")
        self.play(Create(vector_v))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        self.place_at_grid(vector_x, "D4")
        self.play(Create(vector_x))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(colors[3])
        # Dual space placeholder
        dual_text = Text("Dual Space", color=colors[3], font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(dual_text, "B5")
        self.play(FadeIn(dual_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(colors[4])
        self.place_at_grid(camera_icon, "E3")
        self.play(FadeIn(camera_icon))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualization: The Dual Nature", [
            "Visualize the transformation by rotating the vector.",
            "Constant dot products create perpendicular level sets.",
            "These lines reveal the underlying dual landscape."
        ])

        # Define mobjects
        vec = Vector([1, 1], color="#FFD700")
        line1 = Line(start=[-2, 0, 0], end=[2, 0, 0], color="#FFFFFF")
        line2 = Line(start=[0, -2, 0], end=[0, 2, 0], color="#FFFFFF")
        
        # Position them
        self.place_at_grid(vec, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(line1, 'C3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(line2, 'C3', scale_factor=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        # Rotation of the vector and level sets
        self.play(Rotate(vec, angle=PI/4, about_point=self.grid['C3']),
                  Rotate(line1, angle=PI/4, about_point=self.grid['C3']),
                  Rotate(line2, angle=PI/4, about_point=self.grid['C3']))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        # Highlighting the interaction
        self.play(Indicate(line1), Indicate(line2))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Dot products translate geometry into precise numbers.",
            "Vectors act as measuring devices for space.",
            "This synthesis completes our view of duality."
        ])
        
        # Elements for the summary diagram
        circle = Circle(radius=0.8, color="#FFFFFF")
        line = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#FFFFFF")
        matrix = Matrix([[1], [0]], element_to_mobject_config={"font_size": 24})
        
        # Initial placement
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(line, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'E4', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Add them to scene
        self.play(FadeIn(circle), FadeIn(line), FadeIn(matrix))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Dot products translate geometry into precise numbers.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.play(circle.animate.set_color("#FF5733"), line.animate.set_color("#FF5733"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Vectors act as measuring devices for space.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.play(matrix.animate.set_color("#FF5733"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # This synthesis completes our view of duality.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.play(
            circle.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), 
            line.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), 
            matrix.animate.set_color("#FFFFFF")
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Dot Products and the Concept of Duality

sections.title: Geometric Intuition: The Projection
sections.content: Define the dot product as a measure of how much one vector 'shadows' or projects onto another. Use a visual of a sun shining directly above one vector, casting a shadow of the other onto a line.
sections.example: A hiker climbing a hill: The dot product shows how much of the hiker's movement is actually 'uphill' versus 'flat distance'.

sections.title: The Algebraic Bridge
sections.content: Introduce the standard formula: a · b = |a||b|cos(θ). Explain that this connects the coordinate-based calculation to the geometric behavior, forming the foundation for duality.
sections.example: Calculating the work done by a robotic arm pulling a crate at an angle to the floor.

sections.title: The Core of Duality: Vectors as Functions
sections.content: Shift perspective: Instead of two vectors, view the dot product as a linear function. A fixed vector 'v' acts as a machine that takes in any vector 'x' and outputs a scalar. This is the dual space concept.
sections.example: A motion-sensing security camera: The camera's orientation is the fixed vector; as a thief (vector x) walks past, the camera outputs a scalar value representing the 'detected intensity'.

sections.title: Visualization: The Dual Nature
sections.content: Show an animation where a vector rotates. As it rotates, the 'level sets' (the points where the dot product is constant) form lines or planes perpendicular to the vector.
sections.example: Contour lines on a map: The vector points in the direction of the steepest slope, while the level lines represent the 'dual' landscape of constant elevation.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Conclude that dot products translate geometric relationships into numbers, and duality tells us that vectors aren't just arrows—they are the 'measuring devices' for the space they inhabit.
sections.example: An artificial intelligence weighting system: Each feature (vector) is multiplied by a weight, essentially projecting the data onto a decision axis.
